name: Microsoft
description: Microsoft sells software and cloud computing to businesses and consumers. The largest profit pool is subscriptions: Microsoft 365 (Office, Teams, security), Dynamics business apps and LinkedIn. The fastest-growing pool is the Azure cloud, where customers rent computing, storage and AI services by usage, plus server software and enterprise support. The rest is Windows (mostly licensed to PC makers), Xbox games and hardware, and Bing and Edge search advertising. FY2026 revenue was $331.8B, and 54% of operating profit came from the Productivity and Business Processes segment even though Intelligent Cloud is nearly the same size in revenue. It holds a large, long-term strategic partnership with OpenAI, and is spending heavily on data centers for AI.

businessLines.name: Productivity and Business Processes
businessLines.how: Per-user monthly or annual subscriptions paid by businesses and consumers for Office, Teams and security add-ons, plus LinkedIn recruiter and ad revenue and Dynamics business-app subscriptions; growth comes from more seats and higher-priced bundles.
businessLines.description: Microsoft 365 commercial and consumer, LinkedIn, Dynamics 365.

revenue.note: Search-coverage figure of the FY2026 10-K segment note; rounded $140.0B on Microsoft's earnings page

businessLines.revenueNote: Search-coverage figure of the FY2026 10-K segment note; rounded $140.0B on Microsoft's earnings page

businessLines.name: Intelligent Cloud
businessLines.how: Usage-based billing for rented computing, storage and AI model hosting on Azure, plus per-server licences and support contracts; growth is capacity-constrained and requires large capital spending on data centers.
businessLines.description: Azure and other cloud services, server products (SQL Server, Windows Server), GitHub, Nuance, enterprise and partner services.
businessLines.marketShare: Azure about 20% of worldwide cloud infrastructure services in Q2 2026, versus AWS 28% and Google Cloud 15%

businessLines.name: More Personal Computing
businessLines.how: A licence fee per PC shipped (Windows OEM), one-time game and console sales plus game subscriptions and in-game purchases, and search ads sold per click or impression.
businessLines.description: Windows OEM licences and devices (Surface), Xbox content, services and hardware, search and news advertising (Bing, Edge).
